chunks: And I say: If this utterance is weighed against any other utterance, after the word of Allah (Exalted is He) and the word of His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), it would prove heavier and superior in every respect.

For example, ‘Ali’s saying “Keep light and over-take” is the shortest expression ever heard with the greatest sense conveyed by it. How wide is its meaning and how clear its spring of wisdom! We have pointed out the greatness and meaningfulness of this phrase in our book al-Khaṣā’iṣ.

key_terms.الْخَصَائِصِ: Al-Khaṣā’iṣ (a book by As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī detailing the unique virtues of the Imams)
key_terms.تَخَفَّفُوا تَلْحَقُوا: Keep light and over-take (a phrase encouraging spiritual and practical lightness to advance in life)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the phrase 'Takhaffafu talhaqu' in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Raḍī elevates ‘Ali’s (a.s.) concise advice to 'lighten up so you may overtake' by weighing it against all human discourse, declaring it superior in depth despite its brevity. This commentary underscores the Shia scholarly appreciation for *ījāz* (conciseness) as a vessel for profound wisdom, linking the physical act of traveling light to spiritual detachment. The reference to *al-Khaṣā’iṣ* situates this insight within the broader tradition of highlighting the unique virtues (*khawāṣṣ*) of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.sayed-ali-raza: as-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: If this utterance of ‘Ali (a.s.) is weighed with any other utterance except the word of Allah or of the Holy Prophet, it would prove heavier and superior in every respect.

For example, ‘Ali’s saying “Keep light and over-take” is the shortest expression ever heard with the greatest sense conveyed by it. How wide is its meaning and how clear its spring of wisdom! We have pointed out the greatness and meaningfulness of this phrase in our book al-Khaṣā’iṣ.
